Mild sodium nitrite intoxication is generally associated with symptoms related to methemoglobinemia, as sodium nitrite can convert hemoglobin to methemoglobin, which reduces oxygen delivery to tissues. Common symptoms include:

- Cyanosis (bluish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes due to lack of oxygen)
- Drop in blood pressure
- Reflex tachycardia (increased heart rate to compensate for low blood pressure)
